title: Why the limit
description: Too much current can damage a part even when the loop is complete. A safe limit is a ceiling, not a target you try to hit.

blocks.md:
## Too much current

Current is not a score you maximize. If current goes past the cap, wires and the lamp heat up. Brightness is one goal; safe current is the other. In this one-cell loop, current is about 1 / ohms. The cap we gave you is 2, so ohms of 1 gives current 1 (bright enough and under the cap) while ohms of 0.25 gives current 4.

This bites when you chase the brightest looking setting and pick 0.25 or 0. The lamp may look great in a sloppy model, then the constraint fails. Heat is the real-world version of that failure.

![A fuse sits on the loop](assets/fuse-loop.svg)

```text
battery → resistor(1 Ω) → lamp → battery
current ≈ 1 / 1 = 1    (under the cap of 2)
```

A common mistake is setting resistance to 0 so current is huge. The question asks which move is safer when you want a brighter lamp.

blocks.promptMd: You want a brighter lamp. Which move is safer in this one-cell loop?

choices.md: Set resistance to 0 so current is huge

blocks.explainMd: Brightness rose at ohms=1 without crossing 2. 0.25 looks brighter in a sloppy model but fails the constraint.

hintLadder.md: 1 / 1 = 1, which is bright enough and safe.

blocks.promptMd: Sort these currents. The cap is 2.
